long_biography.plain_text:
Steam changed Valve from a game studio into a direct platform linking developers, publishers and players. Newell built the company around Half-Life, then made its sequel dependent on Steam, accelerating adoption of the distribution service. Keeping Valve private left him able to direct its games, software and hardware without public shareholders.

Newell co-founded Starfish Neuroscience to develop minimally invasive interfaces with the brain and body. The company uses a flat, self-directed team structure and is developing devices intended to move from laboratory work towards clinical use. Its research programmes span neurological, psychiatric and oncology applications.
